the-battle-of-calatafimi
Garibaldi's volunteers, the Thousand, storm a hill at Calatafimi in Sicily in May 1860 and beat a larger Neapolitan army, a key victory on the way to uniting Italy. Remigio Legat painted it in 1860.
the-thin-red-line

The 93rd Highlanders stand in a thin line against the Russian cavalry at Balaclava on October 25, 1854, refusing to retreat, and a newspaper called it the 'thin red line'. Robert Gibb painted the famous moment in 1881.
the-battle-of-sinop

The Russian navy sets the Ottoman fleet ablaze at Sinop in November 1853, a night battle that helped bring about the Crimean War. Ivan Aivazovsky, Russia's famous painter of the sea, painted it with glowing flames.
the-battle-of-the-alma-1854
French and British soldiers climb the hills above the Alma River on September 20, 1854, the first big battle of the Crimean War. Hippolyte Bellangé painted the assault in 1855.
the-battle-of-the-alma-20-september-1854
Eugène Lami paints the Battle of the Alma in 1855 with a wide, pale view of the hills where the French and British armies attacked Russian positions.
the-capitulation-of-kars
After a long siege, the Ottoman fortress of Kars surrendered to the Russians in November 1855 after its defenders ran out of food. Thomas Jones Barker painted the surrender around 1860.
charge-of-the-light-cavalry-brigade-25th-oct-1854

On October 25, 1854, British light cavalry rode straight down a valley into Russian cannons in the Charge of the Light Brigade, immortalized in Tennyson's poem. William Simpson, a war artist, drew this view the next year.
the-taking-of-the-malakoff
French soldiers plant the tricolor flag on the Malakoff tower on September 8, 1855, the attack that finally brought down Sevastopol. Horace Vernet painted the victory in 1858.
fighting-in-the-gorge-of-the-malakoff-8-september-1855
French troops fight hand-to-hand in the trenches of the Malakoff fortress in September 1855 in the final attack on Sevastopol. Adolphe Yvon painted this huge battle scene in 1856.
the-return-from-inkerman

Tired, silent Grenadier Guards trudge back after the Battle of Inkerman in 1854. Elizabeth Thompson, later Lady Butler, painted this sad picture of the cost of war in 1877, when she was becoming one of Britain's best-known battle painters.
the-siege-of-sevastopol
The Russian painter Grigory Shukaev shows the defense of Sevastopol during the long siege of 1854 and 1855, one of the longest sieges of the Crimean War.
the-battle-of-sinop-alexey-bogolyu
Alexey Bogolyubov paints the burning ships of the Battle of Sinop in 1860, a few years after the Russian navy destroyed the Ottoman fleet there in 1853.
cavalry-at-balaklava

A wide view of the cavalry battle at Balaklava in October 1854, drawn by William Simpson, who traveled with the army to the Crimea as a war artist. His images were printed to show the war to people at home.
the-anti-slavery-society-convention-1840

Delegates from many countries pack a London hall at the World Anti-Slavery Convention of 1840, where women were not allowed to take part, an event that helped start the women's rights movement. Benjamin Robert Haydon painted the meeting in 1841.
a-ride-for-liberty-the-fugitive-slaves

A family of enslaved people flee on horseback in the early light of the Civil War. Eastman Johnson painted it in 1862 after seeing such an escape, and it is one of the first great American paintings to show the bravery of people escaping slavery.
the-first-reading-of-the-emancipation-proclamation-by-p
President Lincoln reads the first draft of the Emancipation Proclamation to his cabinet in July 1862. Francis Bicknell Carpenter painted this meeting in 1864, and it hung in the US Capitol.
the-abolition-of-slavery-in-the-french-colonies-27-apri
Crowds cheer in the French colonies as slavery is abolished on April 27, 1848, with a flag raised and people embracing. François-Auguste Biard painted the celebration in 1849.
a-visit-from-the-old-mistress

A white woman visits former slaves on a plantation in Virginia after the Civil War, and the women's faces show different feelings. Winslow Homer painted this quiet scene about freedom and its limits in 1876.
abraham-lincoln-george-p-a-hea
President Abraham Lincoln, who led the Union during the Civil War and issued the Emancipation Proclamation, sits deep in thought in this 1869 portrait by George P. A. Healy.
portrait-of-jean-baptiste-belley-deputy-from-saint-domi

Jean-Baptiste Belley, a former slave who became a deputy to the French National Convention for Saint-Domingue (now Haiti), leans on a bust of an antislavery writer. Anne-Louis Girodet painted him in 1797, three years after France first abolished slavery.
thomas-clarkson
Thomas Clarkson, who gathered evidence against the slave trade and traveled across Britain to campaign for abolition, sits writing in this portrait painted in 1788.
slave-market-in-brazil

People who have been enslaved are held for sale at a market in Brazil, which received more enslaved Africans than any other country in the Americas. Johann Moritz Rugendas, a German artist who traveled there, made this picture in 1835.
emancipation-the-past-and-the-future

A circular scene in the center shows a Black family at home in freedom, surrounded by scenes of slavery on one side and a hopeful future on the other. Thomas Nast made this print in 1863, after the Emancipation Proclamation.
harriet-beecher-stowe
Harriet Beecher Stowe, whose novel Uncle Tom's Cabin of 1852 sold millions of copies and made many Northerners see the cruelty of slavery, in a portrait painted in 1853 by Alanson Fisher.
the-battle-of-antietam
Union and Confederate soldiers clash at Antietam on September 17, 1862, the bloodiest single day in American history. Thure de Thulstrup made this scene for a famous set of Civil War prints in 1887.
the-battle-of-gettysburg
The Union army holds a long ridge while the Confederates attack across the fields at Gettysburg in July 1863, the turning point of the Civil War. Thure de Thulstrup made this view in 1887.
the-battle-of-shiloh
Soldiers fight through smoke and trees at the Battle of Shiloh in Tennessee in April 1862, an early and very bloody battle of the Civil War. Thure de Thulstrup painted it in 1888.
the-battle-of-gettysburg-pickett-s-charge
Confederate soldiers cross a wide field in Pickett's Charge, the last big attack at Gettysburg on July 3, 1863, which failed. Peter Frederick Rothermel painted this huge picture in 1870.
the-battle-of-hampton-roads
In March 1862 the ironclad warships Monitor and Virginia fought the first battle between armored ships, changing sea warfare forever. This color print was made in 1889.
bombardment-of-fort-sumter-charleston-harbor
Cannon fire lights up Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor on April 12, 1861, the first shots of the American Civil War. This lithograph was published by Currier and Ives soon after.
sherman-s-march-to-the-sea
General William Tecumseh Sherman's Union army marches across Georgia in 1864, destroying railroads and supplies to break the Confederacy. This engraving was made by Felix Darley in 1868.
the-battle-of-mobile-bay
Union ships under Admiral Farragut steam into Mobile Bay in August 1864, where he is said to have shouted 'Damn the torpedoes!' Julian Davidson made this color print in 1886.
the-battle-of-franklin-november-30-1864
A Union line holds against waves of Confederate attackers at the Battle of Franklin in Tennessee in 1864, one of the last big Confederate attacks of the war. This color print was made in 1891.
abraham-lincoln-cooper-union-portrait

Mathew Brady took this photograph of Abraham Lincoln in New York on the day he made his famous Cooper Union speech in February 1860. Lincoln later said that the speech and the photo helped him become president.
a-harvest-of-death-gettysburg
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed the battlefield at Gettysburg in July 1863, showing the true cost of the war. It is one of the most powerful early war photographs.
the-battle-of-chickamauga

Confederate and Union soldiers fight in the woods at Chickamauga, Georgia, in September 1863, one of the largest and bloodiest battles of the Civil War in the West. This color print was made around 1890.
fort-laramie

Tipis stand by a trading fort in Wyoming, where trappers and Native American traders met and where the Oregon Trail passed. Alfred Jacob Miller, who first visited the Rockies in 1837, painted this view around the 1850s.
daniel-boone-escorting-settlers-through-the-cumberland-

The frontiersman Daniel Boone leads a group of pioneers through the Cumberland Gap into Kentucky, with a woman riding a white horse. George Caleb Bingham painted this hopeful image of westward settling in 1852.
lewis-and-clark-meeting-indians-at-ross-hole

The explorers Meriwether Lewis and William Clark, who crossed the continent in 1804 to 1806, meet the Salish people at Ross' Hole in what is now Montana. Charles M. Russell painted it in 1912 for the Montana Capitol.
the-driving-of-the-last-spike

On May 10, 1869, the last spike joined the Union Pacific and Central Pacific railroads at Promontory, Utah, creating the first railroad across America. Thomas Hill painted the crowd at the ceremony in 1881.
the-oregon-trail

Wagons wind through a glowing landscape under a red sky on the Oregon Trail, the long route that tens of thousands of settlers took west. Albert Bierstadt, famous for his big Western landscapes, painted it in 1869.
boone-s-first-view-of-kentucky
Daniel Boone and his friends look out over the green land of Kentucky for the first time in 1769, in a painting that made the frontier look wide open. William Ranney painted it in 1849.
buccaroos
Cowboys, also called buckaroos, ride in the open West in this lively painting by Charles M. Russell, who worked as a cowboy himself before he became an artist. He painted it in 1902.
herd-quit
Two cowboys race on horses to catch a runaway steer, in a scene full of speed and dust. Charles M. Russell painted it in 1897, drawing on his years working as a cowboy in Montana.
chinese-railroad-workers-in-the-sierra-nevada

Thousands of Chinese workers built the Central Pacific Railroad through the Sierra Nevada, digging tunnels and clearing rock by hand, in very dangerous conditions. This print from the 1870s shows the railroad climbing through the mountains.
custer-s-last-stand

In June 1876 the Lakota and Cheyenne warriors defeated General Custer's soldiers at the Battle of the Little Bighorn, one of the greatest victories for Native Americans in the Plains Wars. Edgar Samuel Paxson painted this version in 1899.
the-siege-of-paris

Paris, personified as a woman holding a flag, rises among dead soldiers during the German siege of the French capital in the winter of 1870 and 1871. Ernest Meissonier, who served in the siege, painted it in 1870.
